safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tingling and numbness in the shoulder.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies tingling/numbness in the shoulder; generated describes elbow/arm/hand but does not mention shoulder involvement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting shoulder involvement could slightly mislocalize the sensory distribution (e.g., more proximal radiculopathy/brachial plexus vs distal entrapment), which may affect diagnostic reasoning. However, the note still captures significant unilateral arm numbness/tingling and weakness prompting urgent neurology evaluation, limiting downstream harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the patient reports headaches; generated does not record patient headaches as a symptom (only includes headache as a safety-net trigger).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Headache history can be relevant when combined with focal neurologic symptoms and transient visual loss, potentially influencing urgency and differential diagnosis. In this encounter, escalation and safety-netting were already present, so the omission is unlikely to change immediate management but represents some loss of clinical detail.
